historical_reviews.deepseek: The section name is plausible, but the excerpt neither proves which hot-swap controller/channel it represents nor retains a complete record. Password exposure and absent Web/expected comparison remain material.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Its classification and power-safety boundary are accepted. The present review sharpens HSC controller-versus-board identity, channel/domain attribution and separation from active hot-swap validation.
historical_reviews.related_cases: I2C HSC_BD or live hot-swap behavior records test management paths or power actions; they cannot be counted as the FRU identity result.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 treats exact component/FRU definitions as supplyable readiness inputs, while ED-38 protects logs and power state and reserves the verdict for the engineer.

original_test_intent: Confirm that each required hot-swap controller or HSC board is represented by the correct read-only FRU record, with specification-matching identity/service fields and an equivalent BMC-Web view, without exercising hot-swap or power controls.
original_method: The platform owner maps HSC locations and protected power domains to stable FRU devices, supplies a field oracle, then automation archives the full inventory and compares the mapped records while an operator validates the corresponding Web entries and unchanged rail/controller health.
manual_activity: The power engineer binds each HSC board/controller and protected load domain to its FRU/Web object, approves the required fields and judges whether mismatches affect serviceability. No hot-plug, rail toggle or fault injection is authorized by this row.
required_inputs: HSC board/controller count, location, PN/revision and protected load/channel map
Per-HSC stable FRU device/area and BMC-Web object
Normal rail, inrush-controller and fault-status baseline for non-disturbance evidence
Approved read-only BMC transport and credential policy
Power recovery owner and diagnostic-log retention policy
safety_requirements: Do not infer the HSC instance from a generic Hot Swap Controller label
Retain full inventory and all record boundaries before extracting mapped HSC fields
Do not exercise insertion/removal, load enable, inrush control, fault clear or rail sequencing
Do not issue FRU, PMBus, CPLD, reset, firmware or power writes
Preserve existing SEL/OS logs; do not erase fault history for a read-only FRU test
Protect credentials and redact secrets while keeping evidence fields complete
Stop on rail/current/fault change, HSC disappearance, duplicate identity, BMC anomaly or management-path instability
agent_execution_scope: Verify the exact source and HSC applicability map
Record passive HSC/rail status without changing it
Collect complete raw FRU inventory through approved access
Resolve and compare each mapped HSC record with the field oracle
Prepare exact Web objects for human parity verification
Confirm HSC/rail/BMC/SEL/OS state did not change
Perform no active hot-swap test and issue no verdict
engineer_actions: Provide expected field and normalization rules
Confirm Web mapping and normal controller/rail state
Assess identity or power-domain anomalies and decide the result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Read-only `fru print` is relevant, but the six-line grep view loses FRU boundaries and may collapse multiple HSCs. It cannot validate channel/domain association, expected fields or Web equality and embeds the BMC password in argv.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture the complete FRU inventory through secret-safe approved access, select HSC records by owner-mapped device/area and physical controller identity, compare their full allowed fields and correlate the exact Web objects without invoking any hot-swap control.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: HSC, FRU list, readability/correctness/Web criteria and 10/10-minute estimates are preserved; no active hot-swap stimulus or controller count is introduced.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES HSC TOPOLOGY, FRU MAP AND FIELD ORACLE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Inventory HSC instances and protected domains, archive complete FRU data, validate each stable record against board-service truth, confirm Web presentation and prove controller/rail state remained unchanged.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Disambiguates which HSC is being identified and explicitly prevents the FRU row from turning into a live power/hot-swap test.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A matching label does not prove channel/location or full serial/part data. Conversely, a healthy rail or successful hot-swap operation does not establish correct FRU identity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Passive access is low impact; nevertheless, selecting or servicing the wrong HSC based on a bad FRU association can interrupt a critical power domain.

project_override_considerations: If HSC functionality is integrated into the PDB or another assembly, the project must identify the owning parent FRU and applicability. It may not fabricate an HSC record or use a PMBus/I2C functional result as FRU proof.
expected_evidence: HSC physical location, channel/load domain and parent-board map
Stable HSC FRU device/area and Web object mapping
Full redacted FRU inventory and command status
Per-HSC decoded expected-versus-observed fields and duplicate/missing analysis
Web parity plus unchanged rail/current/fault/HSC/BMC/SEL/OS state
No-write/no-clear audit, recovery disposition and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: This source row consistently names HSC FRU data and a Web comparison. It lacks topology and values but does not require active hot-swap behavior or contradict itself.

blocked_analysis.analysis: HSC identity and passive full-record collection are technically clear. Project topology and expected fields are prerequisites that can be supplied; no irreducible semantic or recovery blocker is present.

review_improvement: Adds HSC instance/channel provenance and an explicit no-hot-swap boundary, so full FRU identity is validated without risking rail control or borrowing evidence from HSC functional tests.
independent_technical_reasoning: HSC is both a component identity and a controller for potentially disruptive power sequencing. This row only asks for FRU data, so the safe interpretation is a passive inventory check tied to each physical controller and load domain. Complete identity fields matter because a generic Hot Swap Controller label may appear more than once; active rail behavior must remain outside scope. After owner mapping, the data path is automatable while Web comparison and verdict remain confirmed by the engineer.
